label: Sixth-edition aphorisms
title: Aphorism § 92
text:
§ 92



But if it be a disease of a rapid course, and if its serious character
          admit of no delay, the physician must content himself with observing the morbid condition,
          altered though it may be by medicines, if he cannot ascertain what symptoms were present
          before the employment of the medicines, - in order that he may at least form a just
          apprehension of the complete picture of the disease in its actual condition, that is to
          say, of the conjoint malady formed by the medicinal and original diseases, which from the
          use of inappropriate drugs is generally more serious and dangerous than was the original
          disease, and hence demands prompt and efficient aid; and by thus tracing out the complete
          picture of the disease he will be enabled to combat it with a suitable homoeopathic
          remedy, so that the patient shall not fall a sacrifice to the injurious drugs he was
          swallowed.
